task: E2E emitted-project builds inherit the ambient CARGO_TARGET_DIR (the isolated per-lane compiler target), forcing a FRESH runtime compile (tokio/sqlx/axum, ~8GB) per lane/build — the dominant wasted compute in the burndown. Decouple in tools/oracle (build_and_run_rust / build_rust_binary): pin the EMITTED-project cargo build to the SHARED ~/.cache/sky-rust-target (runtime compiled once, reused; proven race-free via cargo build-dir lock + unique emitted package names) REGARDLESS of the ambient CARGO_TARGET_DIR — EXCEPT when the current change edits runtime/ (different vendored runtime -> must isolate). Keeps compiler-crate builds isolated (race safety) while sharing the runtime.
notes: Empirically proven safe 2026-07-14 (/tmp/skyc-share-exp: two concurrent emitted builds to the shared target, both exit 0, lock-serialized, tokio not recompiled). Documented in autopilot.sh TARGET-DIR RULE. Build-perf, not a sweep blocker. [progdev-safe] | REFINEMENT (user, 2026-07-14): the mechanism to make shared-emitted-target safe WITHOUT isolation is to PREFIX the emitted package name per consumer (e.g. 'laneB-26-ui-showcase' / 'reviewer-<id>-<example>') so two lanes building the same example become DISTINCT crates -> no same-name/different-source clobber, tokio/sqlx/hyper reused. Caveats to encode: (1) cargo whole-target build-lock serializes concurrent invocations (removes the correctness race, not a throughput win — builds queue on the lock); (2) a runtime-EDITING lane still collides on the same-named sky_runtime crate -> such lanes MUST isolate the emitted build too; (3) unique names accumulate crates in the target forever -> periodic prune needed; (4) sccache ALREADY dedups the COMPUTE across isolated targets (tokio = cache-hit), so isolation's real cost is DISK not CPU — the rename's win is reclaiming disk + dropping the override, not compile time. Compiler crates (skyc + ~20 workspace crates) CANNOT use this (same names, diff source, renaming all path-deps is infeasible) -> compiler target stays per-lane isolated. Net design = HYBRID: isolated compiler target + shared emitted target with per-consumer package-name prefix (unmodified-runtime lanes only).

task: Reused-by-value generic param clone gap (SEAL): a generic/wildcard type-param used MORE THAN ONCE in a BY-VALUE kernel call moves twice -> cargo E0382 (borrow of moved value). Minimal repro: dup x = toString x ++ toString x -> skyc-0, emits fn main_dup<T1: Clone + Display>(x: T1) with basics_to_string(x) TWICE, no .clone() -> E0382. Root cause: clone_class(IrType::Generic(_)) => CloneClass::NonClone (sky_lower/src/lower.rs:828), so the T5 multi-use-clone pass (fires only for CloneOk) skips generic params, AND reject_fn_value_reuse is a no-op for Generic (ir_contains_fun(Generic)=false), so a reused generic silently moves twice. Fix (guardian-approved sound): in the T5 param loop, treat a reused IrType::Generic(tv) as clonable (insert .clone() on all-but-last use) IFF the emitted bound-set for tv includes Clone (it always does for emitted generics) — the T: Clone bound is the gate (a non-Clone Box<dyn Fn> instantiation fails the Clone bound at the caller before the .clone() is reached, so no unsoundness). Single source of truth: the T5 clone-decision and the bound-map's Clone emission must agree.
notes: Filed by #186 agent (2026-07-14). PRE-EXISTING gap (reachable for ANY by-value kernel on a reused generic), NOT introduced by #186 — #186's Display bound merely makes the narrow double-toString instance reachable (before it died at E0277 first). #177's Db.get* reuse does NOT hit this because db_get_* takes &row (borrows). Loud cargo-fail (E0382), never silent-wrong-accept, so it does NOT block #186's SEAL. Guardian ruled: file separately, own commit (touches the T5 generic-clone contract, broader surface than #186's bound map). Consider a distinct CloneClass::GenericCloneBounded variant so 'is this generic clonable' is carried in the type, not re-derived.

task: 38-composite-ui-multibackend cargo-fail (SEAL): E0382 use of moved value 'habit' (concrete non-Copy RecHistoryIdName). The emitter wraps a reused binding as `Arc::new(move |_x| ({ let habit = habit.clone(); Box::new(move |...| ... habit ...) })(_x))` — the INNER `let habit = habit.clone()` sits INSIDE the outer `move` closure, so the outer `move` still captures/moves the ORIGINAL `habit` (the .clone() reads the free outer var under `move`). A later sibling use (StateMsg::RemoveHabit((habit).id)) then hits use-after-move. Root cause: the clone-for-capture must be HOISTED OUTSIDE the `move` closure: `{ let habit = habit.clone(); Arc::new(move |_x| ...) }` so the closure owns the pre-made clone and the original survives for later uses. Interacts with #178's arc_callback_wrap (the Arc wrapper is where the ordering goes wrong). Distinct from #189 (that's GENERIC-param reuse; this is a CONCRETE non-Copy binding captured into a move closure with sibling reuse).
notes: Found by fresh sweep 2026-07-14. Concrete-msg (StateMsg) app. The emitter already hoists correctly for some closures (the day-closure wraps `{ let habit = habit.clone(); {...} }` OUTSIDE) but NOT for the Arc-wrapped input_checkbox callback. Fix the arc_callback_wrap / callback-capture path to hoist the capture-clone outside the Arc move closure. Verify no double-move remains for any reused non-Copy binding. | DONE 2026-07-14 (final sweep 33/33 PASS). 38 E0382 fixed: capture-clone hoisted outside the Arc move-closure so a reused non-Copy binding survives sibling uses.

task: SEAL: reused non-Copy binding captured into a NESTED move-closure in the Task/CLI pipeline codegen -> cargo E0507 (cannot move out of captured var) / E0382 (use of moved value). Emitter does `{ let conn = conn.clone(); Box::new(move |..| .. conn ..) }` but the clone lands INSIDE the move closure (or a sibling use consumes the original) — SAME class as #191 but a DIFFERENT codegen path: #191 fixed the Input Arc-callback wrap; this is the general task_and_then/task_map nested-closure pipeline (CLI/Task shape). Generalize the capture-clone-hoist so any reused non-Copy binding captured into a move closure clones OUTSIDE the closure, across ALL closure-emission sites (Arc-wrap AND task-combinator AND list_map_consume), not just Input.
notes: Found 2026-07-14 via 07-todo-cli port. Loud cargo-fail (never silent-wrong). Cross-ref #191 (Input Arc-wrap clone-hoist, done) and #189 (generic-param reuse clone). Likely one root cause: the closure-capture emitter must hoist capture-clones outside every `move` closure uniformly. | REFERENCE MECHANISM (../sky Rust backend, checked 2026-07-14 per reference-first): the general fix is a whole-body free-VarLocal occurrence counter `collectFreeVarLocalsMulti :: Can.Expr -> Map String Int` (src/Sky/Generate/Rust/Builder/ExprEmitter.hs:468) — scope-aware (lambda/let/letrec/letdestruct binders excluded; case ARMS take MAX not SUM since mutually exclusive; scrutinee SUMS) — feeding a PER-CLOSURE `.clone()` capture-prelude (ExprEmitter.hs:755 '#8 build the per-closure .clone() capture-prelude', multi-sibling-closure handling :703, consumed at closure-emit sites :3922/:3997). It emits `let v = v.clone();` HOISTED OUTSIDE each closure and SKIPS the single/last use via `ecNoCloneVars` (moved, not cloned). MIRROR this: our #191 is only the Input-Arc slice; port the occurrence-counter + per-closure prelude to sky_backend_rust so it fires at ALL closure-emit sites (Arc-wrap AND task_and_then/task_map AND list_map_consume). The case-arm MAX-not-SUM + letdestruct-binder exclusions are load-bearing (over-count -> spurious .clone() -> E0599 on move-only SkyCmd/SkySub). | IMPL-1 INCOMPLETE (2026-07-14, caught by orchestrator build-it-yourself review; agent parked without running the E2E). task: #184 over-constrains the OWNED-value (Box) branch of IrType::Fun rendering with + Sync. emit_types.rs:260/266 stamps `Send + Sync + 'static` on BOTH the Arc branch (shared callback slots — correct) AND the Box branch (owned/linear fn values). notes: Found 2026-07-14 by a user Arc/Box side-question, reference-first check. RISK: (1) a Sky arrow value emitted Box<dyn Fn+Send+Sync> assigned into a runtime Box<dyn Fn+Send> slot is a distinct trait-object type (auto-traits invariant, no implicit coercion) -> E0308; (2) a nested Box<dyn FnOnce> curry chain is Send but NOT Sync -> blanket +Sync rejects it. 33 green examples don't exercise the owned-decoder-value path hard enough to hit it, but 35-composite-generics (Json.Decode-heavy, pending port via #192) likely will. Cross-ref #184 (done). Verify the fix keeps 33/33 green AND unblocks the Json pipeline. Coordinate with #193 (both touch closure emission). | REFRAME (2026-07-14): the +Sync on the Box branch is LOAD-BEARING, not pure over-constraint. It is what lets a boxed callback PARAM (Box<dyn Fn+Send+Sync+'static>) forward into the runtime's Arc<dyn Fn+Send+Sync> UI slot via arc_callback_wrap (the closure Arc::new(move|_x|(f)(_x)) is Send+Sync ONLY if captured f is Send+Sync). Advantages of the uniform bound: (1) one rendering rule, no ownership/escape analysis; (2) slot-agnostic values -> free Box->Arc promotion, no dataflow rejected; (3) concurrency headroom (share &closure across threads); (4) 'static -> no lifetime plumbing. Therefore DO NOT naively strip Sync to 'match the reference' — that regresses #184 (26/37/38: Send-only param can't forward into the Arc+Sync slot). CORRECT FIX = context-sensitive: keep Send+Sync as default (forwardable), emit Send-ONLY only where Sync is genuinely UNSATISFIABLE (nested Box<dyn FnOnce> curry chains / owned Decoder values that flow into runtime Box<dyn Fn+Send> slots and never into an Arc). Detect the FnOnce/decoder-owned branch specifically; leave the callback-forwarding branch at Send+Sync. | PRINCIPLE RE-WEIGH (2026-07-14, per PRINCIPLES.md strict-order + 2 rules + seal): the blanket +Sync on the owned-Box branch has NO advantage that survives the ordering. The 'uniform rule / slot-agnostic / 'static-enables-dyn-Any' pros are (a) forbidden (no dyn Any / no downcast is P3 Soundness + the explicit no-dyn-Any-in-emitted-code law), or (b) low-tier codegen convenience (Readability P6 / Efficiency P4) that the strict tie-breaker subordinates and that cuts against 'emit concrete/precise, not broad', or (c) the visible face of a SEAL violation (over-broad +Sync rejects a legitimately non-Sync FnOnce/decoder value -> skyc-0-then-cargo-fail = P2/P3). The one load-bearing item (#184 Box-param->Arc-slot forwarding) props up a workaround: the reference types a shared callback AS Arc<dyn Fn+Send+Sync> DIRECTLY (sharing invariant in the type = make-invalid-states-unrepresentable + match-the-reference), which removes the need for the Box +Sync entirely. PRINCIPLED FIX (supersedes the earlier 'context-sensitive Send-vs-Sync' note): render shared/msg-callback positions as Arc<dyn Fn+Send+Sync> directly; render owned/linear values as Box<dyn Fn+Send>; add 'static ONLY where the value genuinely escapes into long-lived storage, never to enable erasure. Backend classifies shared-vs-owned per position (as the reference does) — the bound becomes a consequence of the precise container choice, not a blanket stamp. Costs P4/P6 convenience, which the ordering says must yield. Coordinate with #193 (SharedLambda/Arc promotion path).
